headline: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed the County buying two water systems' assets as a package deal; no vote was taken.
meeting.recap: Staff said the County would buy only the systems' assets, not the companies, so it would not inherit company liabilities.[[0:14:48]] Staff said the department needs Council approval to keep moving forward with the PUC process.[[0:17:38]] Staff said revenue estimates did not account for lower water use under the County's higher rate tiers.[[0:32:29]] Staff said the water tanks are in good condition and get yearly maintenance.[[0:33:54]] Staff said both systems' assets are being sold together as a package deal.[[0:48:08]] Staff said they believe the County would get easements (rights to use land) for all assets, not the land itself.[[0:48:38]] Staff said only PUC approval, not CWRM approval, is needed for the purchase itself.[[0:50:42]] A council member said sustainable yield does not mean pumping that much, because water needs to stay in the ground.[[0:59:26]] This was a discussion item, so no vote was taken.[[1:07:16]] The department expects to go before Council Member Sugimura's committee on August 4th.[[1:07:28]] Staff said that if Council acts in August, the purchase could close around April of next year.[[1:08:13]]
meeting.next: Staff hope to have answers to follow-up questions by the August 4th meeting. If approval is received, the item would go to the full Council for final approval. Once Council approves, the department would move forward with the PUC process. Staff said they would double-check that a planned fire station's water needs are covered by existing use permits. A County attorney said they would check whether a right of first refusal is in the easement agreements. Staff said they could try to separate the operating costs for one system's drinking and non-drinking water.
